sources.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information (2018 author-hosted draft)
sources.locator: Chapter 1 §1.1.1, PDF pp.6–7 (tensor products and product inner products); §1.1.2, PDF pp.8–22 (linear maps, tensor maps, trace); Chapter 2 §§2.1.1 and 2.1.3, PDF pp.58–60 and 67–68 (registers and partial trace).

contents.name: Finite register spaces and computational-basis setting
contents.reason: The book formalizes finite registers and compound register spaces. The local definition fixes C^d, the root first-linear pairing, the empty-register convention, and its distinction from C^0.

contents.name: Ordered tensor spaces and product inner products
contents.reason: §1.1.1 gives the product inner product on elementary tensors and the factor-order convention. The local proof establishes the lexicographic product basis and checks zero-dimensional factors under the root convention.

contents.name: Computational basis orthonormality
contents.reason: The source provides the finite-coordinate register context. Orthonormality and basis status are verified directly from the repository coordinate pairing and standard-basis supplier.

contents.name: Finite tensor maps and product bases
contents.support: The source's tensor-map construction agrees with the unique multilinear extension route; the local proof supplies the empty and zero-factor cases.

contents.name: Tensor-product basis and dimension
contents.support: The source gives the finite product-basis interface. The full basis and dimension argument is proved locally from the published module-tensor suppliers.

contents.name: Tensor-map composition, identity, and adjoint rules
contents.support: The tensor-map rules in §1.1.2 support the statement; the local proof derives adjoint equality using the root first-linear convention and finite product bases.

contents.name: Finite partial trace and its coordinate contraction
contents.support: §2.1.3 defines the partial trace as a linear map and gives its finite coordinate-sum formula. The local definition makes fixed factor order and empty sums explicit.

contents.name: Trace characterization and basis independence of partial trace
contents.support: The source's unique multilinear characterization and coordinate formula are compared with the local trace-pairing proof; uniqueness and basis independence are established locally.

contents.name: Partial trace positivity and trace preservation
contents.support: The book uses partial trace to form reduced states. The local proof establishes positivity and trace preservation for every non-negative operator, including zero-dimensional factors.

contents.name: Nondegeneracy of the finite trace pairing
contents.support: The source supplies the matrix-trace convention only. The matrix-unit witness and zero-space case are proved locally.

contents.name: Big-endian integer encoding
contents.reason: The cited register sections do not establish the local big-endian formula. Its bijection and permutation consequence are proved by finite induction.

contents.name: Finite wire permutations
contents.support: The source fixes ordered tensor-factor conventions. The basis permutation, inverse, isometry, and zero-factor cases are proved locally.

contents.name: Bell-vector partial-trace calculation
contents.support: Example 2.8 gives a maximally entangled vector and its reduced operator. The local example writes the two-qubit matrix and computes every partial-trace entry.

sources.reading_verification: The complete relevant passages were inspected in the full 598-page PDF and retained extraction research/quantum-computing-planning/sources/qc_r1/TQI.txt: §1.1.1 pp.6–7, §1.1.2 through the tensor-map and partial-trace constructions, §2.1.1 pp.58–60, and §2.1.3 pp.67–68 including the entry formula and maximally entangled example. Watrous uses an inner product linear in its second argument; all local items state and prove the repository first-linear convention.

sources.title: Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, arXiv:1907.09415v6
sources.locator: Chapter 1 §1.3, PDF pp.7–8 (qubits and registers); Appendix A.6, PDF pp.196–197 (tensor products, adjoints and composition); Appendix A.7, PDF pp.197–198 (trace); Appendix B.2, PDF p.200 (binary representation and most-significant-bit convention).

contents.name: Qubit and multi-qubit register basis conventions
contents.reason: §1.3 describes C^2, ordered tensor factors, and the product computational basis. The local definition makes the zero-qubit and root inner-product conventions explicit.

contents.name: Big-endian binary encoding and bitstring-index bijection
contents.reason: Appendix B.2 states the binary expansion with the leftmost bit most significant. The local theorem proves bijectivity, including the empty word.

contents.name: Tensor-register basis and product inner product
contents.reason: Appendix A.6 and §1.3 supply the ordered product-space and inner-product conventions; the local proof establishes the general finite list and zero boundaries.

contents.name: Tensor-map definition, basis, composition, and adjoint
contents.support: Appendix A.6 states the Kronecker tensor map and its product, adjoint, and parenthesization identities. Local proofs supply the unique-extension and empty-factor arguments.

contents.name: Tensor-product basis and dimension
contents.support: Appendix A.6 states the product-basis dimension formula. The local proof handles empty lists and zero-dimensional factors.

contents.name: Tensor-map composition and adjoint
contents.support: Appendix A.6 gives the matrix composition and adjoint identities. The local proof translates them to the repository's first-linear convention.

contents.name: Finite wire permutation as a basis permutation
contents.support: Appendix A.6 supports ordered tensor labels and matrix conventions; bijectivity and isometry of the factor permutation are proved locally.

contents.name: Matrix trace convention for the trace-pairing lemma
contents.support: Appendix A.7 states the diagonal-sum trace convention. Nondegeneracy is established by the local matrix-unit argument.

contents.name: Partial trace and reduced-state identities
contents.reason: The cited A.6–A.7 and §1.3 passages do not develop partial trace; Watrous and Preskill provide the independent partial-trace treatments.

contents.name: Partial-trace characterization and positivity
contents.reason: No partial-trace proof is taken from this source; the complete local proof uses the trace-pairing lemma.

contents.name: Bell-vector partial-trace calculation
contents.support: The source supplies the EPR vector and register ordering context. The local example computes the matrix and partial trace without attributing that computation to de Wolf.

sources.reading_verification: The complete relevant passages were inspected in the full 239-page lecture-note PDF and retained extraction research/quantum-computing-planning/sources/qc_r1/de-wolf-1907.09415.txt: §1.3, Appendix A.6, Appendix A.7, and Appendix B.2. De Wolf uses source-style bra/ket conventions; the local statements and proofs use the explicitly declared first-linear root pairing.

sources.title: John Preskill, Quantum Computation, Chapter 2: Foundations I: States and Ensembles (updated July 2015)
sources.locator: §2.3, PDF pp.17–19, Eqs. (2.61)–(2.67) (bipartite vectors, reduced density operator, and partial-trace contraction).

contents.name: Partial-trace coordinate formula and reduced state
contents.support: Equations (2.63) and (2.66) contract over the second-system basis. The local definition works for arbitrary finite operators and explicitly covers an empty basis.

contents.name: Trace characterization of a reduced operator
contents.support: Equation (2.62) verifies the reduced operator against every observable on the retained subsystem. The local proof establishes uniqueness and basis independence for arbitrary operators.

contents.name: Non-negativity and trace of a reduced state
contents.support: The source interprets the partial trace as the subsystem density operator. The stronger linear-map result is proved locally for every non-negative input.

contents.name: Bell-vector example and reduced density matrix
contents.support: §2.3 derives the reduced density operator by summing the shared-basis index. The local example computes all four output entries in the chosen two-qubit ordering.
